incidents.vector: State-linked actors compromised telecom signalling infrastructure to siphon call and location data, the campaign that prompted the UK's now-weakened telecoms security code.
incidents.impact: Britain rolled back proposed defenses (independent signalling intrusion detection, monthly equipment reboots, service-account hardening) after industry lobbying; NCSC has confirmed Chinese hackers targeted UK critical-sector organizations, leaving known weaknesses open for years.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of zero-day CVE-2026-20245, an output-encoding flaw letting authenticated or local attackers run commands as root; chaining earlier Cisco zero-days supplies the needed access.
incidents.impact: Seventh actively exploited Cisco SD-WAN zero-day this year, first flagged by Mandiant; no patch or workaround available, with limited cases pushing configuration changes to edge devices.

incidents.vector: Two Russia-aligned clusters weaponized the patched WinRAR path-traversal flaw CVE-2025-8088 via spear-phishing emails carrying malicious archives that drop payloads into Windows Startup locations.
incidents.impact: One cluster deployed the GiftedCrook stealer to harvest credentials and documents; another delivered HTA-based espionage malware via Cloudflare Workers C2, targeting military innovation centers, formations, and law enforcement.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in PAN-OS portal and gateway components allowing unauthorized attackers to establish GlobalProtect VPN sessions.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed probing and a small number of successful gateway-connected sessions; no lateral movement seen yet. Added to CISA's KEV catalog on May 29 with public PoC code now circulating.

incidents.vector: Large-scale password-spraying campaign against U.S. technology firms, part of China-nexus espionage seeking AI capabilities and intellectual property.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike reports a single China-nexus password-spraying campaign impacted more than 340 U.S. entities; China-nexus actors drove over 58% of state-sponsored intrusions against the technology sector, now the world's most targeted industry.

incidents.vector: A previously undocumented group posed as women seeking romance or aid volunteers on Telegram, luring soldiers into installing SafeLoveStealer Android spyware or entering Telegram credentials on spoofed login pages.
incidents.impact: The campaign stole files, photos, location data and live microphone audio, and hijacked Telegram sessions to intercept communications from troops in border regions and combat zones; an internal panel stored intercepted military unit data. Not attributed by researchers.

incidents.vector: DPRK-nexus actors compromised the widely used Axios NPM package — downloaded roughly 100 million times per week — to poison the open-source software supply chain.
incidents.impact: Likely exposed millions of downstream users; part of broader DPRK targeting of developer ecosystems. Tracked by Mandiant as UNC1069 and tied by CrowdStrike to a DPRK-nexus cluster.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; exploitation traced back to at least April 2026.
incidents.impact: ServiceNow quietly patched the platform and notified affected customers, with incidents mainly impacting its Australia platform release.

incidents.vector: Intruders used compromised credentials issued to other government agencies authorized to access land and real estate data to reach the registry.
incidents.impact: About 600,000 records stolen, including real names, cadastral information and real estate-specific property details.

incidents.vector: A ransomware group breached the company's corporate network and is extorting it under threat of leaking stolen data.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim to have stolen sensitive financial documents and listed the company on their leak portal; MyPillow has not confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Zero-day CVE-2026-50751, a critical (9.3) authentication bypass in Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access deployments using the deprecated IKEv1 protocol, exploited in the wild since at least May 7.
incidents.impact: A few dozen organizations globally were targeted; Check Point confirmed at least one case where post-exploitation was tied to a ransomware affiliate also abusing Palo Alto, Fortinet and F5 VPN flaws.

incidents.victim: U.S. legal, professional and financial services firms
incidents.vector: The Silent Ransom group (UNC3753) combined invoice-themed phishing, IT-helpdesk voice impersonation, and even in-person office visits to install RMM tools and abuse BYOD/VDI access for data theft.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations hit between January and May; the group moved from compromise to exfiltration and extortion in under an hour in recent cases, threatening to publish stolen client files and PII. FBI also warned of in-person USB-based intrusions.

incidents.vector: Meta says NSO Group ran a new spear-phishing operation luring WhatsApp users to click malicious links leading to an external site, in violation of a U.S. court injunction.
incidents.impact: Meta disrupted the campaign and filed a contempt motion; it urged lawmakers to keep NSO sanctioned, warning the sanctioned, Entity-Listed firm continues to defy U.S. courts.

incidents.vector: Data extortion actors listed Charter on their dark web leak portal; the telecom subsequently confirmed a security breach.
incidents.impact: Charter confirmed a breach after the ShinyHunters extortion crew named it on its leak site.

incidents.vector: Iranian hackers breached the news agency's website, deleting articles and disrupting online broadcasts.
incidents.impact: The attackers defaced and disrupted the independent all-female outlet and threatened to dox and harm employees.

incidents.victim: U.S. government-linked Instagram accounts (Obama White House, Space Force)
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers tricked Meta's AI customer-support bot into adding an attacker email to target accounts during the password-reset flow, using a VPN IP near the victim's hometown.
incidents.impact: The Obama White House and Space Force senior-enlisted Instagram accounts were briefly defaced with pro-Iran messaging; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no backend database was breached.

incidents.vector: A Shai-Hulud-variant worm (Miasma) compromised 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories, planting config files that auto-execute a 4.6MB credential-stealing payload when repos are opened in AI coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code).
incidents.impact: The automated sweep broke CI/CD pipelines worldwide (notably Azure/functions-action) and harvested developer credentials; tied to the earlier May 19 compromise of Microsoft's durabletask PyPI package. Linked to the broader TeamPCP supply-chain campaign.

incidents.vector: A former IBM threat-intelligence VP alleges in a lawsuit that foreign-government-linked attackers repeatedly breached IBM and AT&T systems over years.
incidents.impact: The whistleblower complaint claims the companies concealed multiple intrusions from the U.S. government and made false security assurances to win and keep federal contracts.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed the university's CareerConnect careers portal at the end of May and exfiltrated stored records.
incidents.impact: Data of alumni, research staff and employers was stolen from the platform used to connect students and staff with recruiters.

incidents.victim: Australian federal MP (Zali Steggall) and staff
incidents.vector: A suspected foreign state actor compromised the WhatsApp account of an independent MP and three staffers in March, believed to be part of a campaign targeting politicians' Signal and WhatsApp accounts.
incidents.impact: The breach, disclosed in June, is unconfirmed but assessed as likely part of a Russian campaign against the messaging accounts of foreign politicians.
